title: Clinical utility of circulating tumor cell PD-L1 expression for predicting immunotherapeutic response and prognosis in esophageal cancer

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Clinical utility of circulating tumor cell PD-L1 expression for predicting immunotherapeutic response and prognosis in esophageal cancer》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · p0025】Liquid biopsy approaches, particularly the detection and characterization of circulating tumor cells (CTCs), offer a promising non-invasive strategy that may complement tissue-based testing [13], [14], [15]. CTCs are tumor cells shed from primary and metastatic sites into the peripheral circulation, and have been proposed as a potentially more integrated assessment of tumor heterogeneity compared with a single tissue biopsy [16]; however, direct evidence that CTC analysis fully captures intratumoral heterogeneity is still limited. Importantly, PD-L1 expression can be evaluated on CTCs (CTC PD-L1), enabling dynamic monitoring of PD-L1 status through serial blood sampling [17]. Emerging evidence in other malignancies, including non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and hepatocellular carcinoma, has demonstrated the predictive potential of CTC PD-L1 for immunotherapy outcomes, with several studies reporting significant associations between baseline CTC PD-L1 positivity and superior objective response rates (ORR) as well as prolonged progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) [18], [19].

【Introduction · p0035】To address these knowledge gaps, the present study was designed to comprehensively evaluate the clinical utility of baseline CTC PD-L1 expression as a predictive and prognostic biomarker in patients with stage III–IV esophageal cancer receiving chemo-immunotherapy. Specifically, we sought to (1) investigate the associations of CTC and CTC PD-L1 status with clinicopathological parameters, including tumor size, clinical stage, and metastatic status; (2) compare the predictive value of CTC PD-L1, tPD-L1, and total CTC burden for objective response in patients receiving chemo-immunotherapy; and (3) assess the prognostic significance of these biomarkers for PFS and OS using Kaplan–Meier survival analyses and univariate and multivariable Cox regression. We hypothesized that CTC PD-L1 expression would demonstrate better predictive and prognostic performance than tissue-based tPD-L1 testing and total CTC enumeration, offering a more dynamic and representative approach to guide immunotherapy decisions in esophageal cancer.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Clinical utility of circulating tumor cell PD-L1 expression for predicting immunotherapeutic response and prognosis in esophageal cancer》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Materials and methods · p0050】This study was a non-interventional, prospective, real-world investigation conducted at the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University (Ethics approval number 2024-KY-0100-002), enrolling patients with advanced esophageal cancer without autoimmune diseases. Participants received at least two cycles of chemotherapy combined with PD-1/PD-L1 blockade immunotherapy starting from April 2024. Patients who received chemotherapy alone were not included in the primary biomarker analysis and were analyzed separately as an exploratory reference group. Peripheral blood samples (10 mL) were collected at baseline (T0) for CTC detection and PD-L1 expression analysis at Zhuhai Sanmedbio (Fig. 1), the effects of response (ORR, PFS, and OS) to combination of chemotherapy and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy and follow-up care are being studied at the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University with more than 3 months.2.Detection and characterization of circulating tumor cells and tissue PD-L1 expression

【Materials and methods · p0060】The LiquidBiopsy™ system (Zhuhai Sanmed Biotech Ltd., Zhuhai, China) was employed for CTC isolation and enrichment, as detailed in Winer J P et al. [20]. In brief, PBMCs were separated from 10 mL of whole blood by Ficoll (ρ = 1.077 g/mL; Solarbio, Cat: P8610) gradient centrifugation at 1000×g for 10 min at room temperature, fixed in 2% paraformaldehyde (Solarbio, Cat: P1110) for 1 h at room temperature, and subsequently incubated with capture cocktail reagents and streptavidin beads (BD Biosciences, Cat: 557812) to immobilized CTCs. The capture cocktail consisted of biotinylated anti-EpCAM (Santa Cruz Biotechnology, Cat: sc-59906; Clone: HEA125)/anti-HER2 (Santa Cruz Biotechnology, Cat: sc-23864; Clone: 24D2)/anti-Trop2 antibody (Hubio, Cat: HA600011; Clone: A5C5), each at a final concentration of 1 μg/mL. For phenotypic characterization, cells were stained with a panel detection kit (Zhuhai Sanmed Biotech Ltd.) consisting of anti-pan CK (Clone: C11), anti-PD-L1 (Clone:28-8), and anti-CD45 (Clone: 2D1) antibodies (each at a final concentration of 4 μg/mL) overnight at 4 °C, with DAPI (Thermo Fisher, Cat: D1306) used for nuclear visualization. To evaluate PD-L1 status, CTCs were incubated with HRP-labeled anti-PD-L1 antibody, followed by anti-HRP IgG Alexa Fluor® 594 secondary antibody (Jackson ImmunoResearch, Cat: 123-585-021). CTCs were identified based on specific phenotypes with threshold of CK mean of fluorescence intensity (MFI) and ratio of CK/CD45, while PD-L1 positivity was defined based on thresholds for both PD-L1 MFI and the PD-L1/CD45 ratio. A patient was categorized as CTC PD-L1 positive upon detection of at least one PD-L1-expressing CTC, whereas CTC positivity was assigned when at least one CK-positive CTC was identified [17]. Tissue PD-L1 expression was examined with 22C3 pharmDx (Dako) and defined as positive at threshold of TPS ≥ 10% [21].3.Response assessment and survival endpoints

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Clinical utility of circulating tumor cell PD-L1 expression for predicting immunotherapeutic response and prognosis in esophageal cancer》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · p0095】A total of 93 patients were enrolled, of whom 63 (67.7%) were CTC-positive and 50 (53.8%) were CTC PD-L1-positive. Among them, 59 patients received first-line of chemo-immunotherapy and constituted the primary analysis cohort; 34 patients received chemotherapy alone and were analyzed separately. The distribution of CTC counts and CTC PD-L1 counts across the overall cohort and clinicopathological subgroups is summarized in Supplementary Table S1. In the overall cohort, the median CTC count was 3 (IQR 1–5; range 0–167) and the median CTC PD-L1 count was 1 (IQR 0–3; range 0–159). Both CTC and CTC PD-L1 counts were higher in patients with stage IV disease (median 4, IQR 1–7 and median 2, IQR 0–4, respectively) and in those with metastasis (median 4, IQR 1–7 and median 2, IQR 0–4) than in patients with stage III disease (median 1, IQR 0–3 and median 0, IQR 0–1) or without metastasis (median 1, IQR 0–3 and median 0, IQR 0–1), whereas no obvious differences were observed by sex or cancer type. The distribution of CTC and CTC PD-L1 positivity across clinicopathological subgroups is summarized in Table 1. Regarding clinical stage, the CTC-positive rate increased progressively from stage III (53.6%) to stage IV (78.8%). A similar upward trend was observed for CTC PD-L1 positivity (stage III: 39.0%; stage IV: 65.4%). In terms of metastasis, patients with M1 (≥1 metastatic site) exhibited significantly higher CTC counts than M0 patients (p = 0.0411, Fig. 2A), with a cutoff of 3 yielding a sensitivity of 73.47% and specificity of 68.18% (AUC = 0.7481, 95% CI: 0.6481–0.8482, p < 0.0001; Fig. 2E). Although CTC PD-L1 counts did not reach statistical significance between the two groups (p = 0.1591, Fig. 2B), the positivity rate was higher in M1 patients (67.3% vs. 38.6%), and a cutoff of 2 provided a sensitivity of 59.18% and specificity of 72.73% (AUC = 0.6818, 95% CI: 0.5731–0.7905, p = 0.0026; Fig. 2F).

【Results · p0100】Tumor size was also associated with CTC detection. Patients with T3–4 tumors had markedly higher CTC positivity (81.8% vs. 48.7%) and significantly elevated CTC counts (p = 0.0454, Fig. 2C) compared with those with T1–2 tumors. At a cutoff of 3, the sensitivity and specificity for distinguishing T3–4 from T1–2 were 70.37% and 69.23%, respectively (AUC = 0.7360, 95% CI: 0.6316–0.8403, p = 0.0001; Fig. 2G). Similarly, CTC PD-L1 positivity was higher in the T3–4 group (66.7% vs. 35.9%), though the difference in CTC PD-L1 counts did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.1829, Fig. 2D); a cutoff of 1 yielded a sensitivity of 66.67% and specificity of 64.10% (AUC = 0.6636, 95% CI: 0.5511–0.7761, p = 0.0073; Fig. 2H). Finally, when stratified by tumor PD-L1 expression, though patients with tPD-L1 ≥10% showed slightly higher rates of both CTC positivity (71.4% vs. 63.6%) and CTC PD-L1 positivity (59.2% vs. 46.5%) compared with those with tPD-L1 <10%, spearman's correlation analysis showed no significant association between tPD-L1 and total CTC counts (rho = 0.091, p = 0.396), nor between tPD-L1 and CTC PD-L1 expression (rho = 0.136, p = 0.200) (Supplementary Table S2). These findings suggest that tissue PD-L1 status and CTC-derived PD-L1 assessment may provide independent or complementary information, rather than reflecting the same biological signal; however, this hypothesis requires more direct validation with paired tissue–CTC samples.2.Correlations between CTC PD-L1, tPD-L1, Total CTC Burden and Immunotherapy Clinical Response

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Clinical utility of circulating tumor cell PD-L1 expression for predicting immunotherapeutic response and prognosis in esophageal cancer》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Fig. 1 · fig1】Fig. 1 Study workflow and patient disposition. A total of 93 patients with stage III–IV esophageal cancer was enrolled in this study. Baseline assessments included CTC isolation with PD-L1 evaluation, tissue PD-L1 expression detection by immunohistochemistry (IHC), and baseline imaging (CT/MRI). Patients were subsequently allocated to receive either chemotherapy alone (n = 34) or chemo-immunotherapy (n = 59). Follow-up was conducted to assess PFS and OS. Statistical analyses were performed to evaluate (1) associations of CTC and CTC PD-L1 with tumor size, clinical stage, and metastasis status, and (2) correlations of CTC and CTC PD-L1 with ORR, PFS, and OS.

【Fig. 2 · fig2】Fig. 2 Baseline CTC and CTC PD-L1 levels stratified by metastasis and T stage, with ROC curve analyses for diagnostic performance. (A–D) Box-scatter plots comparing total CTC counts (A) and CTC PD-L1 counts (B) between M0 and Mx patients, as well as total CTC counts (C) and CTC PD-L1 counts (D) between T1–T2 and T3–T4 subgroups. Statistical comparisons were performed using the Mann–Whitney U test, with p-values of 0.0411, 0.1591, 0.0454, and 0.1829, respectively. (E–H) Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves evaluating the diagnostic performance of total CTC and CTC PD-L1 counts for distinguishing metastatic status (E, CTC; F, CTC PD-L1) and TNM stage (G, CTC; H, CTC PD-L1).

【Fig. 3 · fig3】Fig. 3 Predictive value of CTC PD-L1, tumor tissue PD-L1, and total CTC counts for immunotherapeutic response. (A–C) Stacked bar charts showing the ORR stratified by (A) CTC PD-L1 status (positive vs. negative), (B) tissue PD-L1 expression (positive vs. negative), and (C) CTC positivity (CTC + vs. CTC−). Blue and red bars represent PR and SD/PD, respectively. (D–F) Violin plots comparing the distributions of (D) CTC PD-L1 counts, (E) tissue PD-L1 expression percentage, and (F) total CTC counts between PR and SD/PD groups. Statistical comparisons were performed using the Mann–Whitney U test, with p-values of 0.0237, 0.3554, and 0.1197, respectively. (G–I) Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves evaluating the discriminative performance of (G) CTC PD-L1 counts, (H) tissue PD-L1 expression, and (I) total CTC count for differentiating responders (PR) from non-responders (SD/PD).
